s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive swelling of the manubrium with a history of previous thyroid surgery
salient_findings: Lytic lesion replacing the manubrium on CT imaging
Follicular thyroid cells on fine-needle aspiration
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
Previous substernal left hemithyroidectomy for benign goiter 12 years ago
Swelling of the manubrium is slightly tender
Swelling increased in size over the month prior to presentation
CT imaging shows a lytic lesion replacing the manubrium
Residual right goiter is present
Lytic lesion is in close proximity to the brachiocephalic artery and the left innominate vein
Fine-needle aspiration revealed follicular thyroid cells
Pathological examination shows thyroid follicles infiltrating adjacent to bone trabeculae

shortlist.label: Follicular thyroid carcinoma with direct invasion of the manubrium
shortlist.why_kept: Direct invasion of the manubrium by follicular thyroid carcinoma is consistent with the patient's history of previous thyroid surgery and the presence of follicular thyroid cells in the manubrial lesion.

shortlist.label: Metastatic follicular thyroid carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Metastatic follicular thyroid carcinoma is a possible explanation for the lytic lesion in the manubrium, given the patient's history of previous thyroid surgery and the presence of follicular thyroid cells in the manubrial lesion.

shortlist.label: Papillary thyroid carcinoma with metastasis to the sternum
shortlist.why_kept: Papillary thyroid carcinoma with metastasis to the sternum is a possible diagnosis, although the presence of follicular thyroid cells in the manubrial lesion makes it less likely than follicular thyroid carcinoma.

shortlist.label: Thyroid carcinosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Thyroid carcinosarcoma is a rare and aggressive tumor that could explain the patient's symptoms and the presence of a lytic lesion in the manubrium.

shortlist.label: Insular thyroid carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Insular thyroid carcinoma is a rare and aggressive tumor that could explain the patient's symptoms and the presence of a lytic lesion in the manubrium.

s4.champion: Follicular thyroid carcinoma with direct invasion of the manubrium

raw.champion: Follicular thyroid carcinoma with direct invasion of the manubrium
raw.rationale: The presence of a lytic lesion in the manubrium with thyroid follicles infiltrating adjacent to bone trabeculae, as shown by pathological examination, and the history of previous substernal left hemithyroidectomy for benign goiter, suggests direct invasion of the manubrium by follicular thyroid carcinoma cells.

rejected.label: Metastatic follicular thyroid carcinoma
rejected.why: While possible, the direct invasion pattern and the history of previous surgery in the same area make direct invasion more likely than metastasis.

rejected.label: Papillary thyroid carcinoma with metastasis to the sternum
rejected.why: Fine-needle aspiration revealed follicular thyroid cells, not papillary thyroid carcinoma cells.

rejected.label: Thyroid carcinosarcoma
rejected.why: There is no indication of both carcinoma and sarcoma components in the provided pathological examination.

rejected.label: Insular thyroid carcinoma
rejected.why: The pathological findings do not specifically indicate the presence of insular thyroid carcinoma, which is a rare and aggressive form of thyroid cancer.
